articles.title: Judge Halts Arch Construction: US court blocks Trump monument for 14 days; veterans’ suits proceed
articles.description: A federal judge has placed a temporary hold on the construction of a proposed triumphal arch meant to celebrate American independence. Approved by the National Capital Planning Commission, the monument faced opposition from Vietnam War veterans and local entities, who argued it lacked necessary permissions. As legal disputes unfold, the project’s momentum is halted for two weeks, raising alarms over potential environmental impacts and increased traffic in the area.

articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex jumps 500 points after flat opening, Nifty also rises
articles.full_text: "The Indian market is on a very very strong foundation," Chouhan told ANI, pointing to year-on-year net profit growth of around 19 per cent and an expected CAGR of 15-16 per cent over the next two years. He said second-quarter FY27 earnings have been significantly better than the previous three quarters, while FII inflows have touched nearly $4 billion in recent days, including $1.5 billion in a single session. Chouhan said a possible slowdown in global AI spending and profit booking in technology stocks could redirect foreign capital towards emerging markets such as India. While large-cap IT companies may face near-term growth challenges, mid-sized and smaller IT firms could perform better. Ahead of Sunday's Muhurat trading session marking Samvat 2083, he said some near-term consolidation cannot be ruled out but maintained that "eventually we are expecting the market to move higher". He advised investors to retain exposure to large-cap stocks for stability and remain selective in mid-cap and small-cap stocks. China and Hong Kong stocks fell as a Nasdaq-led tech rout rippled across Asia and fuelled fears the AI boom is losing steam, although bargain hunting helped pare losses in mainland markets buoyed by Beijing's market-supporting measures. China's blue-chip CSI300 Index dropped 1.5% by the midday break, but remained on track to snap a 12-week-long losing streak. The Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.1%. The tech-heavy selloff was initially more severe. Both the tech-focused Star 50 Index and the AI Index slumped as much as 5% before recouping some losses. In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index was down 1%, while the Hang Seng Artificial Intelligence Index tumbled 4%. Overnight, the Nasdaq posted its steepest one-day drop since April 2025, wiping trillions of dollars off market value as investors fretted that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could bring tighter scrutiny of the AI sector. The risk-off mood spilled over to Asia in early hours, with South Korea's KOSPI plunging more than 8% at one point and Japan's Nikkei falling 5%. Dong Baozhen, chairman of asset manager Lingtong Shengtai, said the overnight slump in US tech stocks meant the logic behind the AI-driven rally had crumbled. "The US stock market has been the standard-bearer and backbone of the global AI bull run. Now that backbone has snapped. Can AI bull markets elsewhere hold up on their own?" he said. Chinese AI hardware stocks with significant exposure to the US market were among the hardest hit. Zhongji Innolight , which makes optical transceivers for data centres and generates most of its revenue in America, slumped 8% to a one-year low. Rival Eoptolink Technology tanked 7%. AI software firms also came under pressure, with Zhipu sinking as much as 15.4% amid concerns that a broader AI backlash could threaten the timing of Anthropic's IPO. Jason Hsu, founder and chairman of Rayliant Global Advisors, said China's sentiment-driven stock market was heavily influenced by AI stock performance in the United States, as quoted by Reuters. Technology stocks carry significant weight in China's stock market and "what people are really watching closely is whether AI in the United States is a bubble," he said, adding that any signs of a bubble bursting in the US "obviously will affect the Chinese market." Still, early panic selling drew in bargain hunters, helping trim losses in a market that remains on course for weekly gains after Beijing rolled out support measures and reiterated its commitment to preventing systemic risks. "I don't think China can completely escape the fallout from Wall Street, especially with selling this aggressive," said Pepperstone strategist Dilin Wu. "But I'd be careful about treating China's entire AI supply chain as one trade," she said, adding growth in AI chip players like Huawei and Cambricon are mainly driven by China's push for technological self-reliance. "When investors rush to cut risk, even good companies get sold." The Sensex rose 0.6% to 79,794 and the Nifty advanced 0.35% to 24,621 as of 10:05 am, supported by sustained foreign fund inflows. Indian stocks remained relatively resilient despite a global market sell-off, with limited exposure to major AI-related stocks providing some insulation. The rupee gained 0.1% to 94.38 against the dollar, while government bond yields rose nearly 3 basis points to 7.1988%, pressured by higher oil prices and US Treasury yields. The NSE Nifty 50 was trading at 24,490.10 in early trade, down 46.50 points at 9.24am or 0.19% from its previous close of 24,536.60. The index opened marginally higher at 24,538.20 but soon slipped into negative territory. The BSE Sensex was trading at 79,471.98 in early trade at 9.22 am, up 161.97 points or 0.20% from its previous close of 79,310.01. The index touched an early high of 79,523.61 and a low of 79,016.05. Japan's Nikkei share average plunged 5.3% to 57,858.61 midday break, extending a sell-off in technology and AI-linked stocks amid concerns over tighter regulation and a possible slowdown in AI spending following the Democrats' sweep in the US midterm elections. The index had fallen as much as 7.1% during the session and was heading for its worst daily performance in eight months. The broader Topix also slumped 5.4%, with all 33 industry sectors trading lower. The sell-off followed steep overnight losses on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recorded their biggest daily falls since April 2025. AI-linked stocks bore the brunt, with SoftBank Group tumbling 9.3% and chip-testing equipment maker Advantest falling 4.6%. The Nikkei has declined every day this week and is on track to lose 8.6% for the week, its steepest weekly fall since March 2025. Market volatility has also climbed to its highest level since March 31, as investors reassess AI companies' growth prospects, infrastructure spending and profitability.

articles.title: Three Oklahoma students found their teacher unconscious on concrete after a fall; what they did next earned them a public honour
articles.description: Three Oklahoma high school students have received public recognition for helping their teacher, Tanya Brawn, after she lost consciousness following a fall outside school on October 8. The students immediately called 911, stayed with her and alerted adults, ensuring she received medical attention. Brawn has since recovered and returned to teaching. The Oklahoma County Sheriff's Office honoured the students during a ceremony at the school's football field, praising their calm and responsible response.
